hook: Right idea, wrong timing is still a loss.
beats: Early is wrong until it isn’t.

Add a timing condition.
Pair every idea with a trigger: a level break, a data release or a close above resistance.
Use a time stop.

hook: Plans are worthless. Planning is everything.
sub: Eisenhower’s lesson for your trading plan.
beats: Version your plan.
Date it, number it, keep old copies. Know exactly which rules you traded under.
Change one thing at a time.
Edit with evidence, record why, test for 30 days. Multiple changes tell you nothing.
Edit on weekends only.
Mid-week changes are mood. Weekend edits are decisions.

hook: If you don’t measure it, you can’t fix it.
sub: A line attributed to Peter Drucker.
beats: Track five numbers.
Win rate, average R, expectancy, max drawdown and rule-adherence percentage.
Rule adherence is the lead indicator.
Results lag. Following your rules 95% of the time is the number you control.
Review weekly, judge monthly.
Weekly for habits, monthly for the numbers. Small samples lie.

hook: Check the bond market before you trust the chart.
beats: Currencies chase yield.
When UK yields rise relative to US yields, sterling tends to find support, and the reverse.
Watch the spread’s direction.
Plot the UK-US 2-year or 10-year gap next to cable. Notice when they move together.
Divergence is a caution flag.
If price rises while the spread falls, ask why before you add. One of them is wrong.

hook: Your edge disappears when you’re tired.
sub: Rest is part of the strategy.
beats: Fatigue breeds errors.
Tired traders miss levels, skip stops and chase. Mistakes rise as focus falls.
Cap your session.
Set a maximum number of hours and trades. When you hit it, you’re done.
Protect sleep before key events.
Big data days reward a clear head. Plan rest the way you plan risk.

hook: Five losses in a row? Here’s the playbook.
beats: Check the rules first.
Did you follow the plan? If yes, it’s variance. If not, it’s discipline. They need different fixes.
Cut size by half.
Set the trigger in advance, for example after a 5% drawdown. Smaller size protects capital and confidence.
Resume on clean execution.
Return to full size after a few trades that follow every rule, whatever the P&L.
